discovery: Prediction and identification of kilonovae, establishing neutron-star mergers as a site of r-process nucleosynthesis
motivation: Where the elements heavier than iron are made has been a central open question since Burbidge, Burbidge, Fowler and Hoyle. Metzger and collaborators predicted in 2010 that the radioactive decay of freshly synthesised r-process nuclei in neutron-star merger ejecta powers a distinct transient, the kilonova, and quantified its luminosity and timescale. Kasen and Tanaka independently showed that the enormous opacities of lanthanides make such emission red and long-lived, providing a specific spectral fingerprint of heavy-element production. When the optical and infrared counterpart of GW170817 appeared in 2017, it matched these predictions closely, giving the first direct observational evidence that mergers produce r-process material in large quantities. Their work turned nucleosynthesis in mergers into a quantitative, testable problem that links laboratory data on exotic nuclei, such as masses, half-lives and fission properties, directly to astronomical observations.
